title: Granulate Formulation Protocol
author: Andreea S
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bkrpkv5n

steps.title: Grow initial culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate a single bacterial colony into an assay tube containing 5 mL Luria Broth (LB) medium and incubate on an orbital shaker at 200 rev min⁻¹, 30 °C for 18 h.

steps.title: Subculture to reach OD≈1
steps.instruction: Transfer the grown culture to a 500 mL Erlenmeyer flask containing 100 mL fresh LB, add 1 mL of the culture (1 % v/v), and incubate at 30 °C, 200 rev min⁻¹ for 24 h until the optical density approaches 1.

steps.title: Prepare DSM medium
steps.instruction: Add 100 mL Difco Sporulation Medium (DSM; 5 g L⁻¹ peptone, 3 g L⁻¹ yeast extract, 1 g L⁻¹ KCl, 0.12 g L⁻¹ MgSO₄·7H₂O) to a 500 mL Erlenmeyer flask, sterilize at 121 °C and 1.5 psi for 15 min, then pack the sterilized medium in plastic bags and store at room temperature.

steps.title: Add mineral supplements
steps.instruction: To the sterilized DSM add 1 mL each of 1 M Ca(NO₃)₂, 10 mM MnCl₂·4H₂O, and 1 mM FeSO₄.

steps.title: Prepare carrier powder
steps.instruction: Mix talc (carrier) with carboxy‑methyl‑cellulose (CMC) at 1 % w/w, calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) at 15 % w/w, and glucose at 0.25 % w/w to obtain a homogeneous powder.

steps.title: Inoculate carrier and incubate
steps.instruction: Inoculate the carrier powder with the bacterial strain to achieve 1 × 10⁶ CFU mL⁻¹, then incubate at 30 °C, 200 rev min⁻¹ for 72 h.

steps.title: Combine with spore suspension and dry
steps.instruction: Mix the same carrier material with the bacterial spore suspension and dry the mixture at 55 °C for 36 h.

steps.title: Sterilize dried mixture
steps.instruction: Autoclave the dried mixture at 121 °C and 15 psi for 15 min.

steps.title: Pulverize formulation
steps.instruction: Using a sterile porcelain mortar and pestle, pulverize the autoclaved formulation into a fine granulate.

steps.title: Estimate spore concentration
steps.instruction: Measure the optical density of the spore suspension at 600 nm using a tube‑reading spectrophotometer set to an OD of 1.978, which corresponds to 8.5 × 10¹⁰ CFU mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Air‑dry granulate
steps.instruction: Spread the formulation on sterile aluminum foil placed in pans and air‑dry in a laminar‑flow cabinet for 24 h at room temperature, stirring occasionally.

steps.title: Sieve to desired size
steps.instruction: Pass the dried granulate (≈35 % moisture) through a 250 µm mesh sieve to obtain the target particle size.

steps.title: Package granulate
steps.instruction: Pack the sieved granulate into sterilized polypropylene bags, seal them, and store at room temperature until use.

steps.title: Enumerate viable propagules
steps.instruction: Perform a standard dilution plating method: take three 1 g aliquots of the dried powder, suspend each in 99 mL sterile PBST (PBS + 0.05 % v/v Tween 20), stir magnetically at high speed for 15 min, dilute the suspension as needed, plate 0.2 mL onto Nutrient Agar (NA) plates, and count colonies to calculate CFU.

steps.title: Extract fatty acid methyl esters
steps.instruction: Subject wet biomass to saponification, followed by methylation and extraction to obtain fatty acid methyl esters (FAMEs).

steps.title: Analyze FAME profile
steps.instruction: Separate the FAME mixtures using a microbial identification system; the software automatically integrates peaks and reports fatty acid identities and relative percentages.
